sentences.text: The skull of the holotype individual has been estimated to be approximately 800 mm in length.
The type specimen of Thanatotheristes is estimated to have reached a length of 8 meters.
Thanatotheristes is characterized by a single row of evenly spaced ridges on the underside of the maxilla near the antorbital fossa.
The frontal bone features a sagittal crest that extends forward of the supratemporal ridge as a broad, rounded structure.
The prefrontal bone has two prongs that project backward and connect with the frontal bone on the underside of the skull roof.
The holotype individual was not osteologically mature when it died.
Fossils of Thanatotheristes have been found in the Foremost Formation of Alberta, Canada.
A referred specimen was discovered at the Twelve Mile Coulee within the upper Herronton Sandstone of the Foremost Formation.
Thanatotheristes lived alongside medium-sized ceratopsids and small pachycephalosaurids.
Thanatotheristes was significantly smaller than its close relative, Daspletosaurus.
Thanatotheristes is classified within the family Tyrannosauridae.
Thanatotheristes is classified under the class Reptilia.
The type species of the genus Thanatotheristes is Thanatotheristes degrootorum.
The parent group of the genus Thanatotheristes is the tribe Daspletosaurini.
Thanatotheristes degrootorum belongs to the tribe Daspletosaurini, which is a sister taxon to Tyrannosaurini within the family Tyrannosauridae.

The tribe Daspletosaurini is diagnosed by features including a thick subcutaneous surface on the anterior ventral maxilla, a narrow jugal ramus, a maxillary angle less than 65 degrees, a broad and dorsomedially arched prefrontal, a dental chin ventral to the third alveolus, and at least 14 maxillary teeth.
The description of Thanatotheristes led to the establishment of the new clade Daspletosaurini within Tyrannosauridae.
Thanatotheristes lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically between 80.1 and 79.5 million years ago.
Thanatotheristes lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
Some researchers suggest that the unique features of the frontal bone might be inadequate, potentially making Thanatotheristes a species of Daspletosaurus.

A 2020 analysis by Yun suggested that diagnostic features of tyrannosaurid taxa might be inadequate due to wide morphological ranges in frontal bones, potentially invalidating the separation of Thanatotheristes.
